concerns.text: The validation of subspace sufficiency (Phase 5 – Power Analysis & Equivalence Testing) uses a binary mask that is derived from the *same* baseline OPD run (Phase 3 – Parameter‑Delta Extraction & Phase 4 – Mask Construction). Because the mask is built to capture the directions of greatest variance in the baseline’s parameter updates, the subsequent paired TOST equivalence test is not independent of the predictor (the baseline trajectory). This creates a circular validation: the subspace is defined by the very updates whose performance it is later used to reproduce, potentially inflating the chance of equivalence. To break this dependence, the plan should include an independent subspace derivation (e.g., using a held‑out “subspace‑training” split, cross‑validation, or a separate set of seeds) or explicitly justify why the current design does not constitute a tautology.
